human_tolerance.notes: In one English study 71.5% of territories were in gardens, which make up 2% of the area (Wikipedia EN). Light tolerance is an authored judgement.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Pair formation in early spring; two or three broods a year is normal (Wikipedia EN). Males return in March and nests are built in April (FR). End date is authored.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Migrants leave from mid-September to November and return March to May (FR). Fraction is the authored complement of winter_fraction; sedentary western populations stay.

vocalizations.description: A loud, clear run of musical phrases, each repeated two to four times, given from trees, rooftops or other high perches; mimicry is common.
A 'chook-chook' that speeds up and grows harsher as danger increases.
A short, sharp 'tsip' contact call; on migration a thin high 'seep' replaces it.

range.note: Native list = countries with at least 1,000 CC0/CC BY GBIF occurrence records (gbif-country-facet, checked 2026-10-31, all records with occurrenceStatus PRESENT), restricted to the species' Palearctic range described by Wikipedia EN ('breeds in most of Europe ... across Ukraine and Russia almost to Lake Baikal'; winters around the Mediterranean, North Africa and the Middle East) and FR ('nord de l'Anatolie, Caucase, nord de l'Iran'). Excluded: NZ and AU (introduced, listed separately); AX and IM (dependencies within FI and GB); North American vagrants (below threshold); DZ (639) and TN (148), which were listed in an earlier draft and fall below the threshold, so they are not listed here; IS, FO, LB, LY, EG, and other 100-999 countries are not listed. GBIF counts are occurrence evidence of presence, not proof of breeding status. Introduced: New Zealand and Australia (both articles, and GBIF records).

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Wikipedia EN: 'run-and-stop hunting technique on open ground'; powered flight; FR: 'vole ... au ras du sol sur de courtes distances'. Walk is the declared ground gait; no hop is claimed.

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg 0.06774 (Small band: 0.05 to 1 kg).

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of '20 to 23.5 centimetres' (EN). FR gives 22 cm adult length, consistent.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Derived with the BTO typical-lifespan method, ex = Ba + (-1/ln(phi)): the expected total age of a bird that reaches breeding age (BTO BirdFacts Biology page, method text only; the page's licence was not confirmed, so it is not listed as a data source). Inputs: phi = 0.571 (SE 0.087), a UK dead-recovery estimate for Turdus philomelos from Tomson et al. (1997), read from ELEscholer2020_data.csv physical line 885 (X=944), source scholer-survival. Ba = 1 y is an AUTHORED assumption (first breeding in the first year). ex = 1 + 1/(-ln 0.571) = 1 + 1.784 = 2.785, recorded as 2.78 y. Limitations: the Dryad row does not state its age class, so phi is assumed to be an adult annual survival rate; a 30-year dead-recovery series; it is not a maximum or captive value. BTO's species page reports a typical life expectancy of 3 years (adult survival 0.563) and Wikipedia EN repeats 'three years'; both are cross-checks, not inputs. Expected value is a proxy for 'typical'; low confidence.

traits.social.note: 'monogamous territorial species'; 'not usually gregarious'; loose winter groups. structure Pair and group_size [1,2] are a derived summary.

traits.defense.note: Authored from the alarm call ('chook-chook' becoming stronger with danger) and FR 'cherche à se cacher rapidement'. No explicit defence statement in the sources.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: FR 'plutôt solitaire et discrète'; EN describes a garden bird that breeds in gardens. Value 0.35 is an authored estimate.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: nests in 'a bush, tree or creeper' in 'forest with good undergrowth'; shrub_thicket is the closest tag.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrate predation (EN 'especially earthworms and snails'); fruit and seed diet from EltonTraits. Fruit months (Sep-Jan) and seed months (Oct-Mar) are authored judgements: the French article says fruit and berries but gives no months. Nest cup (Mar-Jul) matches the breeding phase.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: EN: in one English study 71.5% of territories were in gardens (2% of area). urban_affinity Adapter follows that. light_max 0.6 is an authored judgement.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Authored placeholder, judgement only. No French or British fraction was found in the sources read. Required by PartialMigration; treat as a modelling assumption.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding start in March: FR 'En mars, les mâles reviennent ... En avril, le couple installe le nid'; 2-3 broods (EN). Breeding end (July) is authored. Absent window 09-15 to 02-28 in FR: departure 'de mi-septembre à novembre' and return 'de mars à mai' (FR); fraction 0.5 is the authored winter_fraction complement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg, nest-bound young fed about two weeks then on the ground for two to three weeks (FR); no stage durations are sourced here, so none are set.

look.note: Authored look from the Wikipedia and FR descriptions: brown upperparts, cream or buff underparts with black spots, warm yellow underwing (EN, FR). Proportions and palette are judgement.

behavior.note: Species-local program bt-song-thrush-v1 (behavior.json): the shared bt-perching-songbird-v1 hops to food and fixes nest months to {3,4,5,7}, which skips June. Feeding is switched to walk (run-and-stop, EN) and fruit/seed branches added (EltonTraits diet). All parameters are authored.
